threads.body: Unwrapping every `getMessageListener()` return also affects calls made inside the JMS provider. OpenDDS's `MessageDispatcher`, for example, dispatches via `consumer.getMessageListener().onMessage(message)`, so this advice gives the provider the original delegate and bypasses `SubscriptionMessageListener`; the message virtual field is never populated and durable asynchronous spans omit the subscription name. Please use a propagation mechanism that does not depend on changing the provider-visible getter result while still preserving application-visible listener identity, and cover provider-style getter dispatch.

replies.body: Addressed in 4e8eb1860bd by removing listener wrappers entirely. The original listener now remains provider- and application-visible, while consumer-specific registration state supplies the subscription name during `onMessage`; consumer, session, and connection closure clear that state.

threads.body: [General] This acquires an application-owned listener monitor while `ConsumerState.start()` already holds its internal monitor. A concurrent `synchronized (listener) { consumer.close(); }` can invert that order: registration waits for the listener, while the close advice waits for `ConsumerState`, deadlocking the application. Use an agent-owned lock for virtual-field initialization instead.

replies.body:
Addressed in cbaa0d551f1033fb92ae190b7237282f8750f8ea.

Analysis: Listener virtual-field initialization now synchronizes on a private bootstrap-owned lock shared by both helper classloaders instead of the application listener monitor. The concurrent close regression tests hold the listener monitor while registration enters advice and closes the consumer, proving that initialization and close no longer invert locks.

Upsides: Removes the application-monitor deadlock path while retaining atomic cross-classloader virtual-field initialization.

Downsides: Listener-state initialization is serialized globally, but it occurs only once per listener and normal lookups remain lock-free.

threads.body: [General] These XA factory methods return `XASession`, `XAQueueSession`, or `XATopicSession`, not `Session`. The advice binds every matched return to `@Advice.Return Session`, so Byte Buddy cannot apply it to XA connection implementations and may reject instrumentation of those classes. Restrict this matcher to methods returning `jakarta.jms.Session` (or instrument each XA wrapper's `getSession()` separately).

replies.body:
No code change.

Analysis: Both JMS APIs declare XASession as a subtype of Session, with XAQueueSession and XATopicSession extending XASession. Byte Buddy's default static assignment can therefore bind each XA factory return to the read-only Session advice parameter, just as Java can assign those subtype values to Session. Restricting the matcher would instead remove the connection-close cleanup that the XA methods require.

Upsides: Retains cleanup coverage for XA-created sessions in both JMS instrumentations without adding redundant wrapper instrumentation.

Downsides: No material downside identified.
